Delft
delft
n. (city of Holland; where William of Orange was assassinated in July 1584)
From Middle Dutch Delf, a ditch or delving, from the canal cut through it.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

Delft was William of Orange's residence and the place of his death. On the tenth of July 1584 Balthasar Gerards, a Burgundian who had come to the house with a forged letter of introduction and money given him for a Bible and a pair of pistols, shot the Prince in the hall of the Prinsenhof; he was the first head of state killed with a handgun. The revolt did not collapse, as Philip had expected: the States General carried it on, and William's son Maurice finished the work. The dictionary records Delft because the assassination is one of the cleanest demonstrations in Protestant history that no man's life is at the disposal of his enemies. “My times are in thy hand” (Psa 31:15) was true of William when the shot was fired, and it is the only ground on which a man can take a position that makes him worth killing.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines providence as the care and superintendence which God exercises over his creatures, to appoint as to fix, to settle, to ordain by decree, and death as that state in which there is a total cessation of the vital functions.

expand to see more

PROVIDENCE, n. The care and superintendence which God exercises over his creatures.

APPOINT, v.t. To fix; to settle; to determine; to ordain by decree or decision.

DEATH, n. That state of a being, animal or vegetable, in which there is a total and permanent cessation of all the vital functions.

DECREE, n. In theology, predetermined purpose of God; the purpose or determination of an immutable Being.

Key Scripture

Psa 31:15 — "My times are in thy hand: deliver me from the hand of mine enemies, and from them that persecute me."

Job 14:5 — "Seeing his days are determined, the number of his months are with thee, thou hast appointed his bounds that he cannot pass;"

Act 4:28 — "For to do whatsoever thy hand and thy counsel determined before to be done."

Psa 116:15 — "Precious in the sight of the LORD is the death of his saints."

Modern Corruption

William of Orange shot at the Prinsenhof in July 1584, and a revolt that did not collapse with him.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The live misuse is the modern treatment of a public assassination as pure contingency — a lone man, a lucky shot, history diverted by accident — which leaves the Christian with nothing to say except that it was a shame. Scripture gives a harder and more useful account.

The principle to recover is that the length of a man's life is fixed by God and is not transferred to his enemies by their intent. The psalmist says it while being hunted: “My times are in thy hand: deliver me from the hand of mine enemies” (Psa 31:15). Job states it as a general law: “Seeing his days are determined, the number of his months are with thee, thou hast appointed his bounds that he cannot pass” (Job 14:5). The greatest murder in history was itself within the decree: wicked men gathered “For to do whatsoever thy hand and thy counsel determined before to be done” (Act 4:28). And the death of such a man is not a loss in God's accounting: “Precious in the sight of the LORD is the death of his saints” (Psa 116:15).

Hebrew eth (H6256), an appointed time; Hebrew choq (H2706), a fixed bound.

Hebrew eth (H6256) — a time, a season appointed; Psalm 31:15.

Hebrew charats (H2782) — to determine, to decide, to cut out; Job 14:5.

Hebrew choq (H2706) — a statute, a fixed limit; Job 14:5.

Greek proorizo (G4309) — to determine beforehand; Acts 4:28.

Hebrew yaqar (H3368) — precious, costly, of great price; Psalm 116:15.

Usage

"“My times are in thy hand” (Psa 31:15) — the Prinsenhof, tenth of July 1584."

"“thou hast appointed his bounds that he cannot pass” (Job 14:5) — the first head of state killed with a handgun."

"“whatsoever thy hand and thy counsel determined before to be done” (Act 4:28) — and the revolt carried on by the States General."
